cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What three retrieval streams does hybrid search with rank fusion combine, and how are the results merged?
cards.answer: BM25 keyword matching (with stemming and synonym expansion), vector search over embeddings, and entity-aware graph traversal — merged with reciprocal rank fusion.

cards.heading: Why rank position, not score
cards.question: Why does reciprocal rank fusion merge candidate lists by rank position instead of raw relevance score?
cards.answer: Because it sidesteps having to calibrate incomparable scoring scales across three different retrieval streams.

cards.heading: Complementary blind spots
cards.question: What blind spot does each of the three streams cover that the other two systematically miss?
cards.answer: BM25 finds exact terms and identifiers embeddings blur; vectors find paraphrases and semantic neighbours sharing no keywords; graph traversal finds relationship-connected items neither text stream can see.

cards.heading: Trigger for adoption
cards.question: At roughly what scale does single-file index navigation stop working, forcing real search to take over?
cards.answer: Around 100-200 pages/sources — past that, the index survives only as a human-readable catalog, not the primary navigation mechanism.

cards.heading: Evidence caveat
cards.question: What is the evidentiary basis for the claim that the fused ensemble beats any single retrieval approach?
cards.answer: A practitioner gist reporting production experience with one memory engine (agentmemory) — it matches wider hybrid-search industry practice but reports no published measurements of its own.
